published_posts.title: Why Do We Procrastinate Even When We know Better?
published_posts.subheadline: You are aware that the deadline is nearing and that the work must be completed. Suddenly, checking your phone, watching a video or doing something completely different becomes much easier. Why is it that we love to put things off?
published_posts.cardSummary: Procrastination is frequently viewed as laziness, but there is more to the psychology of procrastination. It is defined by researchers as needlessly postponing ...
published_posts.bodyContent:
Procrastination is frequently viewed as laziness, but there is more to the psychology of procrastination. It is defined by researchers as needlessly postponing a desired action when there is a potential for harm. Research is becoming more and more associated with the link between procrastination and emotion regulation. Sometimes, we don't want to do something because we don't want the feeling we get from the result rather than the action itself.

Think of arriving at an assignment and being overwhelmed by it. You don't start, instead you look at social media. This is a short-term discomfort that lasts for a few minutes. That temporary relief can reinforce the habit, making it easier to repeat the behaviour later.

Even clues could be found within the brain. An MRI study published in Psychological Science in 2018 identified the amygdala as a brain area that is associated with procrastination. The people with less action control had a larger amygdala and weaker links between the amygdala and the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, which is part of the brain that controls actions.

But that doesn't mean that a bigger amygdala leads to procrastination. The study found an association, but not a direct cause, and more research is required to understand the mechanisms in the brain, researchers said.

published_posts.title: You May Be Getting More Out of Your Sugar-Free Gum Than Just Breath Freshness
published_posts.subheadline: A long-held belief that artificial sweeteners flow through the body without having any effect on your heart or metabolism is being challenged by new studies.
published_posts.cardSummary: Chewingum(PHOTO: GETTY IMAGES) Chewing gum and other sugar-free items were promoted for years as the guilt-free, safe alternative to sugar that was delicious wi...
published_posts.bodyContent:
Chewing gum and other sugar-free items were promoted for years as the guilt-free, safe alternative to sugar that was delicious without the negative effects on metabolism. According to two distinct investigations, the assumption is no longer valid.

The first followed 17,710 individuals over a 30-year period and was presented at the annual meeting of the European Society of Cardiology. Researchers from Berlin's Charité University Hospital found that those with the highest blood levels of xylitol had a 57% increased risk of heart attack, stroke, or death during a six-year period. Even when blood pressure, smoking, and age were taken into consideration, the association persisted.

Gum and mints are frequently sweetened with xylitol.

That risk remained 18% greater over the whole 30-year period. Dr. Marco Witkowski, the study's author, acknowledged that the results demonstrate "how little we know" about these additions over the long term and suggested a potential mechanism: xylitol may make blood stickier and thicker, increasing the chance of clots.

published_posts.bodyContent:
According to his office, Graham died on Saturday evening following a "brief and sudden illness." Reports indicate that emergency personnel responded to a medical emergency at his Washington, D.C., residence after reports of cardiac arrest.

Sudden Death After Ukraine Visit

Graham had recently returned from Volodymyr Zelensky's office in Kyiv, where he met the Ukrainian president on Friday. There had been no publicly known health concerns before the trip.

President Trump said he had spoken with Graham only hours before his death.

Trump described Graham as a "true American patriot" who would be greatly missed.

From Trump Critic to Trusted Ally

Graham's relationship with Trump evolved dramatically over the years.

published_posts.title: Jeju Police Officer Arrested After 298 Missing-Person Cases Come Under Scrutiny
published_posts.subheadline: A case involving two people later found dead has exposed a much wider problem, prompting authorities to review every missing-person report handled by the officer.
published_posts.bodyContent:
A missing-person case is supposed to trigger a search for answers. On South Korea's Jeju Island, authorities are now investigating how one police officer came to handle 298 missing-person reports, after allegations that he improperly closed cases without properly confirming that people were safe.

The officer, identified by his surname Bu, was arrested on August 25, 2026, on allegations including dereliction of duty, falsifying official electronic records and obstructing official duties. He has denied the allegations, although police said he later partially admitted to falsely telling the boyfriend of one missing woman that he had contacted her and confirmed she was safe.

The scandal began to unravel after two missing-person cases handled by Bu were found to have been closed prematurely. One involved 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran, who disappeared in May. Police later found a body believed to be hers on August 24, around 104 days after she went missing. Investigators found no call records supporting Bu's claim that he had spoken with her.

Another case involved a man in his 60s who had also been reported missing. His body was found after the case had allegedly been closed without proper confirmation of his safety.

published_posts.title: The Hush-Hush Demands and Phony Endorsements That Rocked the NBA
published_posts.subheadline: A representative for NBA superstar Kawhi Leonard wanted extra money beyond league rules. An investigation says that the Los Angeles Clippers went to extreme lengths to accommodate him.
published_posts.cardSummary: The NBA had just shut down due to the global pandemic when a star player’s business manager approached the Los Angeles Clippers with an unusual demand.While are...
published_posts.bodyContent:
The NBA had just shut down due to the global pandemic when a star player’s business manager approached the Los Angeles Clippers with an unusual demand.

While arenas sat empty and the sport sat idle, a representative for Clippers superstar Kawhi Leonard named Dennis Robertson wanted $10 million more dollars a year for his client. Never mind that the team, owned by former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer, was already paying Leonard the maximum allowed under the NBA’s salary-cap rules.

published_posts.subheadline: The Vikings are betting that former No. 1 draft pick Kyler Murray can be their starting quarterback. And there’s almost no downside: His previous team is footing most of the bill.
published_posts.cardSummary: By the end of last season, the Arizona Cardinals decided that they’d seen enough of their franchise quarterback. They were so ready to get rid of him that they ...
published_posts.bodyContent:
By the end of last season, the Arizona Cardinals decided that they’d seen enough of their franchise quarterback. They were so ready to get rid of him that they were willing to eat tens of millions of dollars to cut him loose.

Now, the Minnesota Vikings are betting that when it comes to Kyler Murray, one team’s potential blunder could be another team’s bargain.

published_posts.subheadline: Plus, Elon Musk’s Boring Co. pushes investors for business help, and America has arrived at the Age of Millionaires
published_posts.cardSummary: 1. FROM MY DESKJohn Fetterman’s blue-collar wardrobe and plain-spoken progressivism once made him a star. Now, the Pennsylvania senator is showing little intere...
published_posts.bodyContent:
1. FROM MY DESK

John Fetterman’s blue-collar wardrobe and plain-spoken progressivism once made him a star. Now, the Pennsylvania senator is showing little interest in doing his job beyond cultivating relationships with conservative media figures and advocating for Israel. Interviews with more than a dozen former aides and lawmakers, along with internal records, show an increasingly dysfunctional operation as Fetterman churns through staff and dodges constituents. With a pivotal election looming that could give him outsize influence in Congress, Will Hobson and Siobhan Hughes report on the senator’s shifting politics—and his growing distance from fellow Democrats.

published_posts.title: ‘By Any Means’ Review: Mark Wahlberg’s Gangster for a Good Cause
published_posts.subheadline: The actor stars alongside Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as a mob hitman enlisted by the FBI to help investigate a racist murder in 1960s Mississippi in this bare-knuckle historical drama.
published_posts.bodyContent:
“By Any Means” suggests it takes a dirty man to clean up a historically and culturally entrenched mess. We’re in 1966 Mississippi, where a straitlaced black FBI agent (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) and a career criminal (Mark Wahlberg) become unlikely partners in an effort to solve a racist murder. Welcome to a race-swapped “48 Hrs.” with a heart of righteous fury.  

Civil-rights dramas tend to be preachy and self-congratulatory, painting halos on the white saviors and the black victims, but the rousing “By Any Means” takes a literally punchy approach. It filters the trauma of race-based suffering through a genre piece about busting heads. Setting out to rebut the sanctimony of, say, “To Kill a Mockingbird,” with its holy glow, the feature directed by Elegance Bratton (“The Inspection”) has more of a “Dirty Harry” vibe. In a system corrupted by racism, justice is sometimes unattainable. If they mess with you, notes Mr. Wahlberg’s character, you’re allowed to mess with them, except he uses a different verb than “mess.”

published_posts.title: American Workers Have Slammed the Brakes on Switching Jobs
published_posts.subheadline: The country is adding around 80,000 jobs a month, up from last year, but workers are still wary
published_posts.bodyContent:
American workers are staying put. 

Workers across all sectors are switching jobs about as infrequently as they were in the years when the job market was still clawing its way back from the 2008-09 financial crisis. The “separation” rate, which includes both people who are laid off and those who leave their jobs voluntarily, has been stuck around its lowest levels since the years after the financial crisis. The flip side of that, the hiring rate, is similarly low.

published_posts.title: What to Know About Mail-Ballot Allegations Against the Postal Service
published_posts.subheadline: An anonymous complaint and fast-moving litigation challenge Trump administration’s claims that it can implement rules without disruption
published_posts.cardSummary: A Democratic senator on Tuesday released whistleblower allegations that the U.S. Postal Service has botched its implementation of mail-in ballot restrictions, a...
published_posts.bodyContent:
A Democratic senator on Tuesday released whistleblower allegations that the U.S. Postal Service has botched its implementation of mail-in ballot restrictions, a move that comes as the Trump administration plays defense in court over the legality of the new regulations.

The litigation could be back in front of the Supreme Court in a matter of days or weeks, casting uncertainty over a method of voting used by one in three Americans that nevertheless has come in for sharp criticism by President Trump.

published_posts.title: An $88,600 Photo With Trump: GOP Hopes to Raise Millions During Convention
published_posts.subheadline: Republican National Committee plans pair of high-dollar fundraisers during this month’s midterm convention in Dallas
published_posts.cardSummary: WASHINGTON—Republicans are planning to raise millions of dollars during the coming GOP midterm convention in Dallas, including asking donors to pay more than $8...
published_posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—Republicans are planning to raise millions of dollars during the coming GOP midterm convention in Dallas, including asking donors to pay more than $88,000 for a photo with President Trump.

The Republican National Committee sent out invitations this week to a pair of fundraising events during the convention. A roundtable with Trump on Sept. 9 will cost $250,000 a person to attend, according to the invitation, which was reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. Donors can also take a photo with the president for $88,600.

published_posts.title: House Passes Measure Funding Government Past the Midterms
published_posts.subheadline: Republicans and Democrats are eager to avoid another shutdown drama as they focus on re-election
published_posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—The House overwhelmingly passed a bipartisan resolution to fund the government past a Sept. 30 deadline, with both Democrats and Republicans eager to avoid a shutdown and leave Washington as soon as possible to campaign ahead of the midterms.

The resolution, which passed 370-48, extends current funding levels through Dec. 11. The Senate passed the stopgap spending bill last month, and it now goes to President Trump’s desk.

published_posts.title: Pro-Business Leader Wins Re-Election in Zambia Vote Marred by Fraud Allegations
published_posts.subheadline: H.H., as supporters call him, plans to triple copper production by 2031
published_posts.bodyContent:
KAMPALA, Uganda— Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema, the pro-business leader of Africa’s No. 2 copper producer, won a second five-year term in a vote marred by opposition allegations of fraud and repression.

The 64-year-old economist and rancher, who entered the race widely expected to win, secured 61.4% of five million votes cast, well ahead of his closest rival, Brian Mundubile, who garnered 38%, the Electoral Commission of Zambia announced Tuesday. The wide margin of victory allowed Hichilema to avoid a runoff.

published_posts.subheadline: A Telemundo executive and an Ecuador intelligence chief are among the victims
published_posts.cardSummary: Seven people, including five Americans, were killed in a helicopter crash in Kenya Wednesday, according to the State Department and local officials.The aircraft...
published_posts.bodyContent:
Seven people, including five Americans, were killed in a helicopter crash in Kenya Wednesday, according to the State Department and local officials.

The aircraft went down in Samburu County, Kenya, about eight hours north of Nairobi, a State Department spokesperson said. Seven people were aboard the helicopter, which crashed around 9:13 a.m. local time, according to Kenya’s Civil Aviation Authority. Samburu County Police Commander David Nkoroi said all seven died at the scene.

published_posts.title: Washington’s Deadly New Headache: an al Qaeda-Houthi Terrorist Alliance
published_posts.subheadline: One man helped broker an arms trade between two militant groups that threatens another key oil-shipping route in the Middle East
published_posts.bodyContent:
On a balmy evening, Jibril “One-Armed” Yahya Ali and his new bride set out for a honeymoon drive along the beach outside al-Ghaydah, Yemen. 

Jibril, a Somali, and his Yemeni wife had met through a mutual acquaintance, an arms dealer who helped Jibril buy military-grade weapons from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. Jibril would then smuggle the arms to al-Shabaab, an Islamist insurgent group fighting to overthrow the government in Somalia.

published_posts.title: The Thai Town Hosting the USS Abraham Lincoln After a Grueling Deployment
published_posts.subheadline: About 5,000 sailors flush with cash and looking for R&R will pour into the seaside resort
published_posts.bodyContent:
PATTAYA, Thailand—At the Hottuna Bar in this seaside town, owner Suchet Teewiang will open a second counter to serve up ice-cold beers. Other venues on Walking Street, the city’s main drag, are staging DJ nights or bringing in extra hands to welcome the expected crowds.

Some 5,000 American sailors will pour into Pattaya starting Wednesday, when the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier and two other Navy ships make a five-day port call in eastern Thailand.
